const rows = $input.all();
const totalRows = rows.length;
const slot = ((totalRows - 1) % 16) + 1;

const mailboxes = [
  { slot: 1,  from: \your@email.com',  name: 'Denver',  company: 'Offshore Staff' },
  { slot: 2,  from: \your@email.com',    name: 'Denver',  company: 'Remote Staff' },
  { slot: 3,  from: \your@email.com',    name: 'Kriza',   company: 'Remote Talent' },
  { slot: 4,  from: \your@email.com',      name: 'Denver',  company: 'Remote Team' },
  { slot: 5,  from: \your@email.com',       name: 'Mae',     company: 'Staff Remote' },
  { slot: 6,  from: \your@email.com',    name: 'Denver',  company: 'Team Offshore' },
  { slot: 7,  from: \your@email.com',     name: 'Mae',     company: 'Offshore Staff' },
  { slot: 8,  from: \your@email.com',   name: 'Kriza',   company: 'Offshore Staff' },
  { slot: 9,  from: \your@email.com',       name: 'Mae',     company: 'Remote Staff' },
  { slot: 10, from: \your@email.com',     name: 'Kriza',   company: 'Remote Staff' },
  { slot: 11, from: \your@email.com',         name: 'Mae',     company: 'Remote Team' },
  { slot: 12, from: \your@email.com',       name: 'Kriza',   company: 'Remote Team' },
  { slot: 13, from: \your@email.com',    name: 'Denver',  company: 'Staff Remote' },
  { slot: 14, from: \your@email.com',     name: 'Kriza',   company: 'Staff Remote' },
  { slot: 15, from: \your@email.com',       name: 'Mae',     company: 'Team Offshore' },
  { slot: 16, from: \your@email.com',     name: 'Kriza',   company: 'Team Offshore' }
];

const mailbox = mailboxes[slot - 1];
const prevData = $('Parse Contact').first().json;

const subjects = [
  'quick question',
  'can I ask you something',
  'not sure who handles this',
  'random idea',
  'quick thought',
  'worth 5 minutes?',
  'one for you',
  'quick one',
  'not trying to sell you anything',
  'is this something you've considered?',
  'built something for electricians',
  'random question',
  'no pressure, just curious',
  'quick favour to ask',
  'saw this and thought of you',
  'figured I'd ask'
];

const bodies = [
  'Hey there,

Just wondering if {{firstName}} is looking at a way to automate Google reviews. We've recently built a system for a few electricians and was curious if it's something you've considered.

We also automate other bits depending on what you need — missed calls, follow ups, quotes, whatever's eating your time. Just hit reply and let me know.

Cheers,
Gunjan',
  'Hey there,

Random one — does {{firstName}} have a system for getting Google reviews after a job, or does it mostly rely on customers remembering?

We built something simple that handles this automatically. Also happy to look at other bits worth automating if reviews aren't the main thing slowing you down.

Reply and let me know either way.

Cheers,
Gunjan',
  'Hey there,

Not sure if you're the right person to ask, but wondering if {{firstName}} has looked into automating Google reviews. We've recently built a system for a few electricians and thought it might be worth flagging.

Also happy to chat about other stuff worth automating in the business if this isn't the main thing on your radar.

Hit reply and point me in the right direction if it's someone else.

Cheers,
Gunjan',
  'Hey there,

Random one — we build automation for trades, starting with automatic Google review requests after a job's done. No chasing, no admin.

If reviews aren't your biggest gap, happy to look at whatever is — missed calls, follow ups, quotes, that kind of thing.

Just hit reply and let me know what'd help most.

Cheers,
Gunjan',
  'Hey there,

Had a quick look at {{firstName}}'s Google profile — solid ratings, but review count seems lower than it should be for how long you've been running.

We built a system that fixes this automatically. Also do other automation depending on what you need — happy to hear what's actually a pain point for you.

Reply and I'll send more info.

Cheers,
Gunjan',
  'Hey there,

We help electricians automate Google review requests after every job — no admin, no chasing. Fair, straightforward pricing, and tailored to how {{firstName}} actually runs.

If reviews aren't your biggest gap, tell us what is — we build around what's actually needed, not a fixed package.

Just hit reply.

Cheers,
Gunjan',
  'Hey there,

Simple one — we automate Google review requests so they go out the moment a job's complete. No extra work for you or your team.

We also tailor the setup depending on what {{firstName}} actually needs automated — reviews are just where most people start.

Reply if you want a look.

Cheers,
Gunjan',
  'Hey there,

Does {{firstName}} currently ask customers for Google reviews after a job, or is it more of a "hope they remember" situation?

We built a simple fix for this — automatic request, no manual follow-up needed. Also do other automation depending on what's actually useful for you.

Just hit reply.

Cheers,
Gunjan',
  'Hey there,

Genuinely just want to show you something first. We built a system that automatically asks customers for a Google review once a job's done — real customers only, no gaming Google's rules.

If it's not useful, no dramas. If it is, happy to also look at other things worth automating for {{firstName}}.

Reply and I'll send more detail.

Cheers,
Gunjan',
  'Hey there,

Just wondering if {{firstName}} has looked into automating Google reviews. We've recently built a system for a few electricians and thought it might be worth flagging.

Also happy to chat about other stuff worth automating in the business if this isn't the main thing on your radar.

Hit reply and let me know.

Cheers,
Gunjan',
  'Hey there,

We recently put together an automated review system specifically for electricians — job's marked done, customer gets a text with the review link, no admin needed from your team.

Wondering if this is something {{firstName}} would find useful. We also tailor it to other stuff depending on what's actually eating your time.

Just hit reply if you want a look.

Cheers,
Gunjan',
  'Hey there,

Rather than pitch straight away — what's the most annoying manual task in the business right now? For a lot of electricians it's chasing reviews, but might be something else for {{firstName}}.

We build automation around whatever that actual pain point is. Reply and tell me what it is.

Cheers,
Gunjan',
  'Hey there,

When someone's got an electrical issue, they check Google Maps and call whoever looks most trustworthy — takes about 30 seconds, and reviews are the main thing they're scanning.

We automate the review-request side of this so {{firstName}} isn't relying on manual follow-up.

Reply if you want to see how it'd work. No pressure either way.

Cheers,
Gunjan',
  'Hey there,

Small favour — mind if I ask how {{firstName}} currently handles Google reviews? Manual ask on the job, or not really a system at all?

We built something that automates this, and depending what you say, might also be able to help with other stuff — missed calls, follow ups, quotes.

Reply whenever suits.

Cheers,
Gunjan',
  'Hey there,

Set up an automated review system for an electrician recently — job marked complete, customer gets a text with the review link, one gentle follow-up if no response in 48 hours. Reviews went from a trickle to steady flow within a month.

Would something like this help {{firstName}}? Reply and I'll share more.

Cheers,
Gunjan',
  'Hey there,

Figured I'd ask — is automating Google reviews something {{firstName}} has thought about? We built a simple system for this recently and it's been working well for a few electricians.

Fair pricing, and tailored to whatever you actually need automated — reviews are just where most people start.

Just hit reply.

Cheers,
Gunjan'
];

const subjectIdx = Math.floor(Math.random() * 16);
const bodyIdx = Math.floor(Math.random() * 16);

const fullName = prevData.fullName;
const emailBody = bodies[bodyIdx].replace(/\{\{firstName\}\}/g, fullName);
const subject = subjects[subjectIdx];

return [{ json: { ...prevData, slot, fromEmail: mailbox.from, senderName: mailbox.name, company: mailbox.company, rowNumber: totalRows + 1, subject, emailBody } }];
